en.html:
...At any rate, the direction of the fight seemed settled. This stubborn fellow had heavy armour to hide behind, so bringing him down would be hard work. But unless I became impatient and presented him with an opening, there was hardly a way for me to lose.

Unless. Such a small word, carrying so much trouble. I had a reason for impatience. Someone probably under the same flag as this enemy might, at this very moment, be attacking Prince Maidono at Kenchouji.

Think of that, and the fire started prickling low in my belly. The biggest enemy, finally, was my own mind. Outside enemy, inside enemy. Excellent arrangement.

Calm. Above all, keep calm. Rush the move and get beaten, and what exactly had I saved?

……兎も角も趨勢は定まったと云えるだろう。
　重装甲を恃んで執拗に食い下がる敵騎を<ruby>降<rt>くだ</rt></ruby>すのは骨
だが、こちらが焦って隙を見せでもしない限り、まず
負ける要素はない。

　<ruby>尤<rt>もっと</rt></ruby>も、それはそれで充分に難儀ではある。
　焦るべき理由がこちらにはあった――目の前の敵と
おそらく同じ旗を仰ぐのであろう誰かが建朝寺の舞殿
宮を今まさに襲っているかもしれないのだ。

　そう思えば、腹の下に焦燥の火が<ruby>ちりちり<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>と<ruby>燻<rt>くすぶ</rt></ruby>る。
　つまるところ最大の敵は自分自身の<ruby>精神<rt>こころ</rt></ruby>に他ならな
かった。

　冷静さの維持が何より肝要だ……。
　手を急いで打ち負かされては元も子もないのだから。

Now. When everything was already too late.
